description: Put this mailbox in warmup, or resume a paused warmup where its ramp stood. Warmup trades ordinary mail with other mailboxes in the pool: 10 a day at first, 1 more each day, up to 40. warmup.todayCap on the answer is how many it sends today. A mailbox back from a quarantine or block sends 50% less warmup, further apart, for 3 days from the next warmup message it sends, even when its health reads healthy: warmup.health.probation says until when. A mailbox that only receives never sends one, so nothing slows it. With receiveOnly: true the mailbox only receives: other mailboxes write to it and it sends no warmup. To resume, pass the same receiveOnly as the first start. To switch between the two, stop its warmup first. A send-only mailbox can't warm up (409): warmup needs a mailbox that receives mail. Needs the send permission, because it makes the mailbox send mail. So an owner's limits on your API key apply here too: a key limited to some mailboxes starts warmup only on those, and a key limited to transactional email starts none (403, with the limit in `details.scope`). Warmup email never counts toward a key's emails a day or in all.

idempotencyKey.description: Your own id for this one call, such as a UUID, up to 255 characters. If the call fails with no answer, call again with the same key and the same arguments: within 24 hours, a saved answer comes back instead of a second run. A call left unanswered can run again after 15 minutes, so a send also keeps its intentKey or draft revision.

receiveOnly.description: true: the mailbox only receives warmup. Other mailboxes write to it and it sends none. Left out, it sends and receives.

name: start_mailbox_warmup
title: Start warming a mailbox
